abstract.p: The poem reflects that a life cut short soon after birth loses only a small amount of pleasure but avoids a much greater span of suffering, presenting early death as a release from the sorrows of life.

editorialDecl.p: Transcriptions are semi-diplomatic, based on on a single manuscript witness. Original punctuation is retained. Letterforms are modernized for u/v and i/j, and majuscule "F" is used in place of "ff". Abbreviations and brevigraphs are expanded, with supplied letters italicized, except for the ampersand. Regularization is applied where it clarifies meaning, using <choice>, <orig>, and <reg>. However, we do not attempt to exactly mirror the layout of the page, nor are we able to reproduce every brevigraph (symbols, strokes, or modified letter forms), mark of punctuation, or symbol accurately.

lg.l: He that is borne to day
Looses some monthes houres of sweete
